Aggregate EPICv2 Probes to Base Probe IDs

Source: R/module_utilities.R
aggregate_beta_epicv2.Rd

EPICv2 arrays report multiple measurements per base CpG probe (e.g., cg06373096_TC11, cg06373096_TC12, ..., cg06373096_TC110 all measure cg06373096). This function aggregates repeated measurements into a single representative value per unique probe ID.

Usage

aggregate_beta_epicv2(beta_df, method = c("median", "mean"))

Arguments

beta_df

A data.frame with a TargetID column (probe IDs) and numeric columns (beta values, detection p-values, etc.). Can be coerced from matrix.

method

Character, one of c("median", "mean"). Aggregation method for numeric columns. Default: "median".

Value

A data.frame with the same structure as beta_df, but with:

  • TargetID column: base probe IDs (suffixes removed)

  • Numeric columns: aggregated values (median or mean across replicates)

If no EPICv2-style suffixes are detected (_[TB].\d+$), returns beta_df unchanged (with a message). In both cases the attribute aggregation_report holds a data.frame (metric, n, description) counting the identifiers: input_rows, output_ids, replicate_groups_collapsed (base IDs built from two or more rows), replicate_rows_collapsed, suffix_stripped_single (base IDs from a single suffixed row), unchanged_ids (IDs without a replicate suffix, kept as they are), malformed_kept (IDs with surrounding white space or an underscore suffix that is not a replicate suffix; kept unchanged), malformed_dropped (missing or empty IDs; removed), all_missing_cells (aggregated values that are missing because every replicate was missing) and all_missing_ids (output IDs missing in every column).

Details

The function detects EPICv2 probe suffixes matching the pattern _[TB].\d+$ (e.g., _TC11, _TB01). If found, the suffix is stripped and values are aggregated by base probe ID. Numeric columns are aggregated using the chosen method, ignoring missing values; a group whose values are all missing stays missing. All other columns are dropped.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
  # Load EPICv2 beta matrix
  beta_df <- read.delim("epicv2_beta.txt")
  
  # Aggregate to base probes
  beta_agg <- aggregate_beta_epicv2(beta_df, method = "median")
  
  # Check result
  dim(beta_agg)  # Fewer rows (unique base probes)
} # }
